title: The bare-PATH bun lookup class QCLI-471 left open: bunx in package scripts, and bare bun in the scripts/*.mjs the check chain runs
description:
Filed from QCLI-471's review (opum-workflow:review-assignment, attempt 2 and attempt 3 findings; job-0u7ratk), folded into one task at the team lead's instruction. QCLI-471 converted package.json's scripts to name the runtime as "$npm_execpath" so a nested command cannot fall back to PATH's bun. Two pieces of the SAME bare-PATH-lookup class were left open; both were measured by the reviews and re-checked here.

1. `bunx` is deliberately exempted in QCLI-471's guard and its case table (test/qcli471-declared-bun-nesting.test.ts treats "bunx tsc" as a non-offender), yet `bunx` is itself a PATH-resolved executable. A future package script containing a bare `bunx` would silently fall back to PATH's bun exactly as a bare `bun` did -- the class QCLI-471's guard exists to prevent. No current script invokes `bunx`.

2. The bare `bun` spawn the change removed from package.json still exists in the scripts/*.mjs the check chain itself runs. scripts/test-repository-check-scope.mjs spawns ("bun", ["run", command]) and is invoked by package.json's `test` script, which `check` runs; scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs and scripts/deliver-package-artifacts.mjs spawn bare `bun` too. On a host whose PATH bun is not the declared pin, these use PATH's bun. QCLI-471's two ACs did not cover them and its commit message scoped the fix to "package.json's scripts", so this is a scope note rather than an overclaim.

Fix direction is not prescribed. Whatever this task does must reconcile with QCLI-471's guard: it currently asserts that no package script invokes a bare `bun`, and its case table pins `bunx` as a non-offender, so widening the guard's rule and its negative cases is part of the work rather than a contradiction of it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: No command reachable from `bun run check` resolves a bun from PATH: package scripts invoke neither a bare `bun` nor `bunx`, and the `bun` spawns in scripts/test-repository-check-scope.mjs and in scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs and scripts/deliver-package-artifacts.mjs name the declaring runtime rather than a bare `bun`.

plan: 1. Replace the bare spawn("bun", ...) with the declaring runtime (process.env.npm_execpath ?? process.execPath) in scripts/test-repository-check-scope.mjs, scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs and scripts/deliver-package-artifacts.mjs.
2. Widen QCLI-471 BARE_BUN to catch a bare bunx, move "bunx tsc" from the negative cases to the positive ones, and update the guard comments.
3. Add a test asserting the three named scripts contain no quoted bun/bunx executable literal and do name the declaring runtime.

4. Prove the guard BOTH ways with recorded runs: a package script with a bare bun -> red; with a bare bunx -> red; the fixed tree -> green. Mutation proof: drop the bunx clause and show the predicted subset goes red.
5. Run the real bun run check at the landed head; commit, PR, one full review at base = merge base, land into dev.
implementationNotes: Fixed the three check-chain scripts to spawn the declaring runtime (process.env.npm_execpath ?? process.execPath) in place of a bare bun: scripts/test-repository-check-scope.mjs, scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs, scripts/deliver-package-artifacts.mjs. Widened the QCLI-471 guard: BARE_BUN now matches bunx, and "bunx tsc" moved from the negative cases to the positive ones. Added test/qcli492-no-path-bun-in-check-chain.test.ts asserting the three scripts carry no quoted bun/bunx literal and do name the declaring runtime. PROOFS, all recorded: (1) a package script using a bare bun -> guard red naming probe:bare-bun; (2) a bare bunx -> guard red naming probe:bare-bunx; (3) the fixed tree -> green. MUTATION PROOF: prediction made first (only the two bunx positives flip), then reverting bunx? to bun in BARE_BUN turned the shell-position test red at its first bunx case, and a per-case table confirmed exactly the two bunx cases flip while every bun positive and every negative is unchanged. AC CONTROL at runtime with a FAKE bun placed first on PATH: the fixed script exits 0 and never touches it; with the fix temporarily reverted the fake IS used and the script exits 1. bun run check exits 0 at this head (1167 CLI + 45 mod pass, 0 fail).
finalSummary: Nothing reachable from bun run check resolves a bun from PATH. (a) package.json scripts invoke neither a bare bun nor bunx -- already true after QCLI-471; the guard now ENFORCES the bunx half too. (b) The three scripts the check chain runs that spawned a bare bun now name the declaring runtime: scripts/test-repository-check-scope.mjs, scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs and scripts/deliver-package-artifacts.mjs each resolve BUN = process.env.npm_execpath ?? process.execPath. npm_execpath is the declaring bun Bun exports into every nested script (QCLI-471) and covers the node-launched and bun-run cases; process.execPath covers a direct bun <file> launch, which is how CI runs prepublish.mjs. The QCLI-471 guard was widened so BARE_BUN matches bunx and "bunx tsc" moved to the positive cases; a new test pins the three scripts. Verified: guard rejects an injected bare-bun package script and an injected bare-bunx one, and accepts the fixed tree (recorded runs); the mutation proof was predicted before running (only the two bunx positives flip) and confirmed; and an AC control with a fake bun first on PATH shows the fixed script exits 0 and never touches it, while the reverted spawn hits it and exits 1. bun run check exits 0 at this head (1167 CLI + 45 mod tests, 0 fail).
